fields.name: INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - NIGHT (CONFESSION)
fields.purpose: The confession, and the locket revealed.
fields.summary: Marcus confesses he was at the creek the day Ada drowned. The locket revealed.

fields.name: INT. HOLLOW CREEK CHURCH - DAY
fields.purpose: An outside voice names the thing wrongly.

fields.arc_description: From a woman who answers questions with tasks to a woman who says the thing and lets it cost her.
fields.backstory: Came west at nineteen. Buried a husband at forty-two and a daughter at fifty-four. Has not left the valley since.
fields.core_belief: Work is what love looks like when you can't speak.
fields.external_goal: Get the homestead through the winter.
fields.flaw: Mistakes silence for mercy — to others and to herself.
fields.greatest_fear: That saying it aloud makes it true forever.
fields.internal_goal: To stop blaming her son without having to forgive him.
fields.motivation: To keep the place standing, and to not have to say aloud what she believes about the day Ada died.
fields.name: Eleanor Cade
fields.summary: Sixty-one, widowed, running the Cade homestead alone since her daughter drowned. Competence is how she holds grief at arm's length.

fields.arc_description: From a man performing ease to a man who says the true sentence and survives the silence after it.
fields.backstory: Was at the creek the day Ada drowned and has never told anyone. Left within the month; sent money, never letters.
fields.core_belief: A debt can be worked off if you work hard enough.
fields.external_goal: Winter over at the homestead and mend what he can.
fields.flaw: Confesses only when cornered, then calls it honesty.
fields.internal_goal: Absolution he cannot ask for directly.
fields.motivation: To be told he is not what he believes he is.
fields.name: Marcus Cade
fields.summary: Thirty-four, back after seven years without warning. Carries his sister's locket and the reason he left.

fields.motivation: To get Eleanor back into the congregation.
fields.name: Reverend Shaw
fields.summary: Buried Ada. Believes grief is a thing you can be walked through on a schedule.

fields.core_belief: Never appears on screen; every design decision about her is an absence decision.
fields.name: Ada Cade
fields.summary: Drowned at the creek crossing seven years before the story opens. Present in the film only as objects: a shawl, a locket, a chime by the door.

fields.name: Eleanor - Marcus
fields.physical_evolution: Arm's length -> post-accident thaw (sc 10) -> ruptured by the truth (sc 19) -> the embrace at the door (sc 24).

fields.key_moments: sc 11 pocketed · sc 19 on the table
fields.name: Ada's locket
fields.narrative_significance: The object that carries the confession. It moves three times and is only spoken about once.
fields.symbolism: What Marcus took from the creek and could not put down.

fields.name: The kettle
fields.narrative_significance: Eleanor's answer to every question she will not take.
fields.symbolism: Work as a way of not speaking.

fields.description: Ada hung it by the porch door the spring before she died. Irregular, slightly flat.
fields.name: Brass wind chime
fields.narrative_significance: Sounds when a door opens. Down in the mud by sc 24.
